questions.prompt: A schema lists `required: ['path']`. The model asks for `read_file` with arguments `{}`. What is true?
options: The provider will refuse to send such a request to your program
The arguments break the schema, and your program has to notice because the schema does not enforce itself
The model will automatically fill in a default path
The request is valid, because `required` only applies to strings
questions.explanation: The schema is a description the model reads as text, not a guard. A missing required argument can still arrive, so your program must check it.

questions.prompt: Why does the wording of a tool's `description` matter so much?
options: It is shown to the user in an error message
The provider uses it to run the function
The model reads it to decide when to use the tool and how to fill in the arguments
It sets the tool's maximum running time
questions.explanation: Schemas become part of the model's input. The description is the model's only explanation of the tool, so a vague one leads to wrong or missed requests.

questions.prompt: You add ten tool schemas to every request. What does that cost you?
options: Tokens in every request, and room in the context window
Nothing, because schemas are sent once and remembered
Only a single charge when the tools are first added
Ten extra HTTP requests per question
questions.explanation: The model is stateless and schemas are turned into input tokens, so they are sent, counted and paid for on every request.
